newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Eurotunnel suspended, advance seen in debt talks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurotunnel suspended, advance seen in debt talks.

text.p: Shares in Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel, racing to restructure its $14 billion debt and head off bankruptcy, were suspended on Monday as progress was reported in crunch talks with its creditors.

"The negotiations are advancing and the positions are getting closer," a source close to the discussions told Reuters ahead of a midnight deadline for the end of a mandate for two court-appointed mediators trying to clinch a rescue package.
"I can't say that there will be an agreement this evening because they are still negotiating. In any case, there is no breakdown," said the source, who declined to be identified.

The Anglo-French company, set up in 1987, has been struggling to negotiate a refinancing of some 72 billion francs ($14 billion) of junior-ranked, less secure, bank debt and interest since it froze payments to around 225 banks a year ago.

A spokesman for the Paris commercial court, where talks were going on behind closed doors, confirmed mediators Robert Badinter and Lord Wakeham would see their mandate expire at midnight on Monday (2200 GMT).
Court president Jean-Pierre Mattei appointed the mediators in February to help negotiate the restructuring and extended their term in June and August. But a new extension is unlikely.
Even after the mediation ends, talks could still continue at the court's discretion, as the debt standstill called by the company last year technically runs until March 14.
A Eurotunnel spokeswoman said it had asked for its shares to be suspended in Paris, London and Brussels to avoid speculation and the creation of a "false market" in the stock.

Eurotunnel shares had closed in Paris on Friday at 9.15 francs per share, compared with an all-time high of 120 francs and a 1987 flotation price of 35 francs. The company's British-quoted shares were worth 114 pence.

In London, an analyst specialising in high yield securities, Mary-Ellen Collins of BDS Securities, said she was confident Eurotunnel would settle restructuring terms soon. "I am confident that a deal could be put together, maybe today, maybe by the end of the month," she told Reuters Financial Television.
The likeliest solution was an immediate debt-for-equity swap that dilutes 50 percent of existing shares and a possible further dilution through the issue of convertible bonds, she said.

Although an outline financing has been roughly agreed between Eurotunnel and its six negotiating lenders, they have been unable to agree pricing of the debt conversion and convertible bonds which would lighten its loan payments.

Jean Salwa, vice chairman of the French Adacte Eurotunnel shareholder association, told Reuters its objective for the conversion price was 35 francs per share, which is the price at which Eurotunnel was floated on the Paris stock market in 1987.
If the banks were to get the stock too cheaply, say five francs per share, Adacte would fight the deal, he said. Any agreement with the banks needs shareholder approval.

Lawyer Georges Berlioz, who acts for Adacte, said it was possible the court could put Eurotunnel into insolvency protection if no agreement is reached. That would hurt the banks more than the shareholders, he said.
"The banks would be indisputably heavily penalised by an insolvency procedure," Berlioz said.
But Didier Renaudin, spokesman for another Eurotunnel shareholder group, thought the chances were a deal could be done. "I don't see any interest for the banks not to do a deal."
The London Times newspaper reported 26 agent bank lenders of Eurotunnel would meet on Friday, October 4, to look at latest proposals for dealing with the company's mountain of debt.

The talks are being led by four commercial banks -- Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP), Credit Lyonnais, Midland Bank, a unit of the HSBC banking group and National Westminster Bank Plc. Two European lending institutions are also involved in the talks -- the European Coal and Steel Community and the European Investment Bank.
